is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated the efficacy of Mosquito Shield™ in preventing landing and blood-feeding of wild, free-flying, pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l. (Page 2)

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions the Vgsc L1014F (kdr) mutation on page 2, but this is a citation of previous work (reference 15: Ngufor et al. 2015) to characterize the study site. No new genotyping of resistance markers was performed or reported in this study.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype counts, allele counts, or frequencies for resistance markers are provided for the mosquitoes collected or tested in this study.

african_field_population.evidence: The experimental hut trial was conducted at a field station in Covè, southern Benin (7°14′N; 2°18′E). (Page 2)

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study evaluating the entomological efficacy of a transfluthrin spatial emanator under experimental hut conditions. (Page 1)

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted at the Covè field station in southern Benin (7°14′N; 2°18′E). (Page 2)

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The trial was conducted in two rounds in 2024: July 10th to August 10th and November 11th to December 10th. (Page 3)

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a standard experimental hut trial at a well-known field station (Covè) and does not indicate overlap with larger genomic datasets like Ag1000G.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary Table S2 is mentioned in the text (Page 8) but likely contains additional bioassay or hut collection data, not the missing genotype data, as molecular methods were not described.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the entomological efficacy of Mosquito Shield™, a transfluthrin-based spatial emanator, against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l. in experimental huts in Covè, Benin. The study reports significant reductions in mosquito landing, entry, and blood-feeding, as well as induced mortality. While it characterizes the local population as having a high frequency of the L1014F kdr mutation, it does so by citing previous literature and does not report any new genotyping data for the mosquitoes collected during this trial.
